newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER WOODS REPORTEDLY ADDS NISSAN OPEN TO BUSY SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS REPORTEDLY ADDS NISSAN OPEN TO BUSY SCHEDULE.

text.p: Tiger Woods will be adding the Nissan Open next month at the Riviera Country Club to his busy early season schedule, according to a newspaper report on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Times said Woods' agent, IMG's Hughes Norton, had confirmed that Woods would compete in the $1.5 million Nissan Open, the same tournament that marked his much-publicised debut in a PGA Tour event five years ago.
The tournament in Pacific Palisades, California, runs from February 27-March 2.

The 21-year-old Woods, who has won three of the 10 tournaments he has entered since turning professional last year, received a sponsor's exemption into the 1992 tournament when he was just 16 years of age.
"Obviously, he's got a soft spot in his heart for the tournament," Norton told the Times.

The Nissan Open would be part of an ambitious early-season schedule for Woods, who last year cited "physical and emotional" exhaustion for skipping the Buick Challenge in Pine Mountain, Georgia after playing four straight PGA events.
Woods is playing in this week's Pebble Beach National Pro-Am alongside move star Kevin Costner, his amateur partner.

He will play tournaments in Thailand and Australia in consecutive weeks and then take a week off before the Nissan Open. Woods is expected to follow with three more consecutive events after the Nissan.

Woods, who turned pro last September, earned PGA Tour Rookie of the Year honours in 1996 after winning two tournaments. He began 1997 with a playoff win over Tom Lehman at the Mercedes Championships and tied for 18th at last week's Phoenix Open.
